message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code and related laws. Below is an overview of key rights you typically enjoy as a renter: | Category | Typical Tenant Rights (Texas) | Notes | |----------|------------------------------|-------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge a security deposit up to one month’s rent for residential units.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | Landlord must provide a written receipt and itemized list of deductions if any. | | **Habitability** | • Landlords must maintain premises in a safe, sanitary condition.
• Must repair major structural issues, plumbing, heating, electrical, etc. | If landlord fails to repair, tenants may withhold rent, repair & deduct, or terminate lease. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Tenants have the right to live without unreasonable interference from landlord or other tenants. | Landlord cannot enter without notice (usually 24‑hour written notice unless emergency). | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑renewal or termination: 30 days’ written notice for month‑to‑month leases; 60 days for longer leases.
• For rent increase: 30 days’ notice for increases less than 10% of current rent; 90 days for larger increases. | Notice must be in writing and delivered personally or via certified mail. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are allowed but must be reasonable (often capped at 5% of monthly rent). | Landlord may not demand payment before the due date. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease agreements must be in writing for leases longer than one year.
• Certain clauses (e.g., “no pets” or “no smoking”) are enforceable if clearly stated. | Oral agreements can be enforceable but harder to prove. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (including public assistance). | This is enforced by the Texas Fair Housing Act and federal law. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlords must follow the legal eviction process: serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for nonpayment), file a lawsuit, obtain a judgment, then sheriff’s execution.
• Tenants can contest eviction in court. | Evictions cannot be carried out by force or lockout without a court order. | | **Repair & Deduct** | • If landlord fails to repair a major issue, tenants may repair it themselves and deduct cost from rent, provided they give notice and keep receipts. | Must be done within a reasonable time and cost must be documented. | | **Right to Access Records** | • Tenants can request copies of lease documents, maintenance records, and proof of insurance. | Landlord must provide upon request. | | **Insurance** | • Landlords are not required to carry insurance covering tenant’s personal property.
• Tenants should consider renters’ insurance. | Some leases require tenants to maintain renters’ insurance. | ### Practical Steps If You Encounter Problems 1. **Document Everything** – Keep written records of all communications, receipts, photos of damage, and copies of notices. 2. **Serve Written Notices** – Use certified mail or hand delivery with a witness for important notices. 3. **Know Your Local Ordinances** – Some cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas) have additional tenant protections beyond state law. 4. **Seek Legal Aid** – If you face eviction or disputes, contact local legal aid organizations or tenant advocacy groups. --- #### Quick Reference Checklist - [ ] Have you received a written lease agreement? - [ ] Is your security deposit returned within 30 days after moving out? - [ ] Are repairs being made promptly when needed? - [ ] Did your landlord give proper notice before raising rent or terminating tenancy? - [ ] Are you aware of your city’s local ordinances that might offer extra protection? If you’re dealing with a specific issue (e.g., landlord refusing to return a deposit, unlawful entry, or discrimination), let me know the details and I can help draft a formal letter or outline next steps.
